context: In the lint pass, reject a verification command that cannot be a shell command - starts with '<', contains an unbalanced angle-bracket placeholder, or fails a shell parse (bash -n). A shell-parse check is the most general and needs no heuristics. Consider whether items whose verification is inherently manual should instead be required to use a self-asserting proxy (e.g. grep for a recorded artifact), which is what the guidance already asks for.
description: A verification ladder command can be a prose placeholder and nothing notices until someone runs it. ducklake-beta-scale-runs-four-modes shipped with rung 1 as '<record the four run ids and correctness-gate outcomes on this item>'; 'todo verify --run 1' died with '/bin/sh: syntax error near unexpected token newline'. Because complete_item() does not gate on verification results, the item still completed with an unrunnable ladder. Sibling of todo-lint-unresolvable-scope-and-ladder-paths, which covers commands naming files that do NOT exist; this is the distinct case of a command that is not a command at all.

preserves.behavior: Existing lint findings keep firing unchanged
Legitimate multi-line or piped verification commands still pass

verifications.command: uv run -- python _project/scripts/todo_db.py lint ducklake-beta-scale-runs-four-modes | grep -qi 'record the four run ids'
